11.0.0.en: Jabin: a title of the king of Hazor, who was the greatest of the Canaanite kings in position in the north.

11.0.1.en: Hazor: a city in northern Canaan.

11.0.2.en: Madon: a city in northern Canaan.

11.0.3.en: Shimron: a city in northern Canaan, located in the portion of Zebulun, 17 kilometers southeast of Nazareth.

11.0.4.en: Achshaph: a city in northern Canaan, located in the portion of Asher.

11.0.5.en: The Arabah: the plain (level land.) Chinneroth: the Lake of Gennesaret, or the Sea of Tiberias, or the Sea of Galilee.

11.0.6.en: The heights of Dor: a city on the shore of the Mediterranean Sea, 15 kilometers from Caesarea of Palestine (Map 4). The east and the west: what is meant is the east and west of the Jordan River.

11.0.7.en: The Amorites, the Hittites, the Perizzites, the Jebusites and the Hivites: Canaanite tribes [see (Gen 10:15-18, Josh 9:1.[)]. Hermon: a mountain located northeast of the Sea of Galilee (Map 4). Under Hermon: at the foot of Mount Hermon (today Mount Sheikh).

11.0.8.en: Mizpah: a city west of Hermon (today the Beqaa), located in the northeast of Palestine. After Joshua's victory over the five kings who lived in the south of Palestine (ch. 10), the chief of the kings of the Amorites in the north moved and sent to his neighbors, the kings of the principal cities east and west of the Jordan, to join together in confronting the coming Jewish danger.

11.0.9.en: Mount Hermon, Merom, Madon, Sea of Galilee, Joppa, Ashdod, Gath, Ashkelon, Hebron, Debir, Gaza, Goshen. Map (4)

11.1.0.en: The waters of Merom: Lake Huleh, which is on the course of the Jordan River and lies 17 kilometers north of Lake Tiberias (Map 4). They gathered very large armies with horsemen and war chariots, and assembled together at the waters of Merom to fight at one appointed time. Perhaps they chose this place because it lay midway between their lands and because of the abundance of its water.

11.1.1.en: The enemy strives to gather his devices and his soldiers to deliver a deadly blow, and God intervenes to make the destruction of the enemy gathered in one place, which is quicker than destroying every city by itself. Just as the enemy has his plans, God has His prevailing plans.

11.2.0.en: To hamstring: to cut the sinews, ligaments and blood vessels of a horse's leg so that it is unable to run and cannot be used in war.

11.2.1.en: The Lord gave Joshua assurance that He would defeat them after one day, so he must not fear. And He asked him to hamstring the horses and burn the chariots, so that the enemies would not use them in new wars in the future, and so that the people also would not use them and rely on them instead of God, as He had commanded them in (Deut 17:16). He set for them a time in which they would conquer the enemies, and this really happened, because the people trusted in God. As for the enemies, they set a time, but they trusted in themselves, so they were defeated.

11.3.1.en: Joshua attacked them suddenly and fell upon them. Here appears the importance of faithfulness in the striving that God supports, so that it succeeds.

11.4.0.en: Zidon: the city of Sidon, between Beirut and Tyre, located on the Mediterranean Sea (Map 4). Misrephoth-maim: it means burnings of water, and it is a place with hot water springs, located 5 kilometers south of Sidon.

11.4.1.en: God delivered them into his hand, so he defeated them, drove them out of the land and destroyed their soldiers, and none of them was able to escape.

11.5.0.en: Joshua did to them what God had asked of him: he hamstrung the horses and burned the chariots.

11.5.1.en: Since God reassures us, let us drive out fear, because everything is in God's hand. Let us only obey His commandments faithfully and carefully, and not be troubled however difficult the surrounding circumstances may be, because God is stronger than everything.

11.6.0.en: He utterly destroyed them: he put them under the ban and killed them, as the Lord commanded, because of their terrible evils.

11.6.1.en: Joshua destroyed the king of Hazor, the leader of evil in the region, and put its people under the ban and burned it, as the Lord commanded. He took all the cities that he had defeated and put their people under the ban, as Moses his teacher had commanded him. But he left the cities that stood on their mounds, because they were naturally fortified and the Jews would benefit from them, so he did not destroy them. He burned only Hazor, in order to remove evil, to frighten the rest, and to show them their weakness, so that they would abandon their reliance on idols.

11.7.0.en: The people took the spoil of the cities and killed their men, as the Lord had commanded Moses. And Joshua carried out completely what Moses had commanded him, and neglected nothing of it.

11.8.0.en: Goshen: it lies in the portion of Judah, 21 kilometers south of Hebron (Al-Khalil) (Maps 4, 5). Mount Halak: a mountain bare of trees near Beersheba, 30 kilometers south of Hebron, and at it Joshua's wars in the south ended.

11.8.1.en: Seir: the land between the Dead Sea and the Gulf of Aqaba.

11.8.2.en: Baal-gad: the name of a city meaning the camp of Baal. It lies on the northern border of Joshua's wars, at the foot of Mount Hermon, and was afterwards called Caesarea Philippi, and today Banias.

11.8.3.en: By Joshua's victory over the kings of Canaan in the north, east and west of Palestine, he took possession of the Canaanite lands in the north and in the south, as is made clear by the places mentioned in these verses and explained above. The wars continued for about seven years, because Joshua was 40 years old when Moses sent him to spy out the land (Josh 14:7); then they wandered in the wilderness 38 years, after which he began to lead the people at the age of 78. And when he divided the land among the people (Josh 14:10) he was 85 years old.

11.8.4.en: The wars lasted a long time for the following reasons:

11.8.5.en: 1- So that the prayers of God's people would increase, and their experience of His power working with them.

11.8.6.en: 2- So that He might give the pagan peoples an opportunity to repent and believe in God.

11.8.7.en: 3- So that God's people would not quickly grow weary from successive wars, which would be beyond their strength.

11.8.8.en: 4- To train His people in patience and endurance.

11.8.9.en: 5- Because if He had driven out the peoples quickly, His people would not have been able to fill their places, and wild beasts would have dwelt in them (Deut 7:22).

11.9.0.en: None made peace with the Jews without war except the Gibeonites, who were one of the tribes of the Hivites. As for the rest of the Canaanites, their hearts were hardened to evil and God left them to their hardness, until God's judgment of extermination was carried out on them. God is not cruel to them; rather He was long-suffering toward them for hundreds of years, and as a result of their many evils He commanded His people to exterminate them.

11.10.0.en: The Anakim: peoples who live south of Jerusalem as far as Hebron, which lies in the south of Palestine, west of the Dead Sea, and which was called Kirjath-arba. They are the giants whom Moses' spies saw and were afraid, and the Lord decreed their wandering 38 years in the wilderness.

11.10.1.en: At that time: after Joshua finished fighting the kings of the north and the south.

11.10.2.en: He cut off the Anakim: he destroyed them.

11.10.3.en: Anab: it lies 25 km south of Hebron, and vineyards were abundant in it.

11.10.4.en: Debir: the religious city of the Canaanites, located near Hebron.

11.10.7.en: Gath: it lies 25 kilometers east of Ashdod. All the preceding cities are Philistine cities (Map 4). Joshua took the land of the Anakim who lived south of Jerusalem and in the mountains that the tribe of Judah took, which are part of the mountains in Canaan that the people of Israel took. So they fled and lived with the Philistines in their coastal cities, such as Gaza, Ashdod and Gath, which Joshua did not take. We shall see that Joshua divided the land among the tribes, and there were no more wars for a long time.

11.10.8.en: God gave His people to possess the Promised Land and to destroy the wicked in it. So He gives you many good things if you walk uprightly before Him, and you live in peace and inherit the Kingdom of Heaven. But if you neglect His commandments you will become troubled like the wicked, and you will have no place with Him in the Kingdom.

11.10.9.en: The borders of the Promised Land

12.0.s.en: (1) The land east of the Jordan

12.0.0.en: The land east of the Jordan is the land that the Jews took by war under the leadership of Moses, and in which the tribes of Reuben and Gad and half the tribe of Manasseh settled. It extends from the valley of the Arnon River in the south, a small river among the tributaries of the Jordan River that flows into it. Its northern border is Mount Hermon (today Mount Sheikh), and it includes the whole Arabah, that is, the valley lying east of the Jordan. It includes the kingdoms of Sihon and Og, in addition to other kingdoms that the tribe of Manasseh took (Num 21, Deut 2:26-37, 3:1-17) (Map 5). Map (5)

12.1.0.en: The land east of Canaan was owned by Sihon king of the Amorites, an ancient people. Its capital was the city of Heshbon, which they had seized from the Moabites (the descendants of Lot.) He reigned over the land from north of the Arnon River, where the city of Aroer is, including the river itself in the middle of the Arnon valley, and the whole valley in which the Arnon River lies, to half of Mount Gilead, which extends east of the Jordan as far as the land of the Arabs and is now called Al-Balqa, and the valley of the Jabbok River on the border of the land of the children of Ammon. These lands were mentioned in (Num 21:25-30).

12.2.1.en: These lands also include the Arabah, that is, the plain extending to the Sea of Chinneroth (the Sea of Galilee) in the north, to the Salt Sea (the Dead Sea) in the south, and Beth-jeshimoth, a city northwest of the Dead Sea (Num 33:49). The southern border was Mount Pisgah, one of the mountains of Abarim east of Jericho, and from Pisgah Moses saw the Promised Land before he died (Num 21:20), (Deut 34:1).

12.3.0.en: Ashtaroth: it lies east of the Sea of Galilee.

12.3.1.en: Edrei: it lies southeast of the Sea of Galilee.

12.3.2.en: It passes along the border of the kingdom of Og king of Bashan, whom the Jews had defeated earlier, and they annexed his land to their country. This land had formerly belonged to the tribe of the Rephaim east of the Jordan, who lived in the cities of Ashtaroth and Edrei and made them their two capitals.

12.4.0.en: It included Mount Hermon (Mount Sheikh) and the city of Salcah, which lies on the eastern border of Bashan at the edge of the southern Druze mountain, and all the plain of Bashan east of the Jordan as far as the border of the kingdom of the Geshurites. Geshur lies south of Hermon, and the Maachathites in the northeast of Palestine beside Geshur (Deut 3:14) (Map 5). Half Gilead, the border of Sihon king of Heshbon: Sihon had taken the southern half of Mount Gilead, and his capital was Heshbon.

12.5.0.en: Moses gave this land as an inheritance to the tribe of Reuben, the tribe of Gad and half the tribe of Manasseh, who wished to take their portion east of the Jordan River.

12.5.1.en: This land points to the portion of the Church of the Old Testament, which did not cross the Jordan, that is, did not receive the blessing of Baptism.

12.5.2.en: God gave His people, the tribes of Reuben and Gad and half the tribe of Manasseh, to possess the land east of the Jordan, on condition that they fight with their brothers to possess the Promised Land west of the Jordan. So if God has granted you strength and resources, help your brothers with them so that they may stand firm in the faith and triumph over Satan, and so have an inheritance in the Kingdom of Heaven.

12.6.s.en: (2) The land west of the Jordan River

12.6.0.en: As for the land west of the Jordan, the Jews took it by war under the leadership of Joshua after the death of Moses and the Jews' crossing of the Jordan River. This land points to the portion of the Church of the New Testament, which enjoyed the blessing of Baptism (the crossing of the Jordan) with Joshua, who is a type of our Lord Jesus Christ. It covers the area from Baal-gad (at Caesarea Philippi) in Lebanon in the north to Mount Halak, that is, the one bare of trees, at Beersheba in the south. This land Joshua gave as a possession to the nine and a half remaining tribes of the children of Israel. It is to be noted that Joshua was humble: he did not attribute the victory to himself as the commander, but to all the people, in order to encourage everyone and make them feel God's work in them.

12.6.1.en: Take care to honor and encourage all who share with you in any work, so that they give all their effort with joy, and you protect yourself from pride and the love of praise.

12.7.0.en: It includes the lands that were in the mountain and the valley and were inhabited by the tribes mentioned. These lands were mentioned earlier in (ch. 9, 11). Joshua was a type of Christ: just as Joshua conquered and took possession of the Promised Land, so Christ also by His death on the Cross opened for us the gates of Paradise and the Kingdom, that we may inherit with Him eternal life in the heavenly Canaan.

12.8.0.en: Jericho: its walls fell by the power of God (ch. 6) (Map 5). Ai: before which the children of Israel were first defeated and then triumphed over it in (ch. 8). The king of Jerusalem, the king of Hebron, the king of Jarmuth, the king of Lachish, the king of Eglon: these are the five kings who went out to fight Gibeon, and Joshua defeated them and killed their kings (ch. 10), and their lands lie in the south of Palestine.

12.8.1.en: Gezer: Joshua took it after his victory over the five kings (ch. 10:33). Debir: Joshua took it after the victory over the five kings (ch. 10:38, 39). Geder: it lies in the far south of Canaan.

12.8.2.en: Hormah: it lies in the south of the land of Canaan (Num 14:45, Num 21:1-3). Arad: it lies in the south of Canaan, 17 miles from Hebron (Num 21:1). Adullam: in the south of Palestine, beside Bethlehem.

12.8.3.en: Makkedah: see (ch. 10:28). Bethel: that is, the house of God, and it lies in the south of Palestine; it is different from the Bethel mentioned in the days of the fathers Abraham, Isaac and Jacob.

12.8.4.en: Tappuah: that is, apple, because of the abundance of apple trees in it, and it lies in the south of Palestine.

12.8.5.en: Aphek: it lies in the plain of Sharon, a fertile plain in the middle of Palestine.

12.8.6.en: Lasharon: it lies southeast of Nazareth by about five and a half miles.

12.8.7.en: Madon: it lies in the mountain in the north of Canaan, and it joined the alliance of the kings in the north to attack Joshua, but he defeated them.

12.8.8.en: Hazor: a city in the north of Canaan, whose king led the alliance against Joshua (ch. 11:1). Shimron-meron: it lies in the north of Canaan and joined the alliance, and they fought Joshua (ch. 11). Achshaph: it lies in the north of Canaan and is among the cities of the alliance (ch. 11:1). Taanach: it lies in the north of Canaan and south of the plain of Jezreel.

12.8.9.en: Megiddo: it lies in the north of Canaan and southeast of Haifa by about twenty miles. Kedesh: it lies north of Hazor in the northern part of Canaan.

12.8.10.en: Jokneam: it lies in the region of Mount Carmel in the north of Canaan.

12.8.11.en: Dor: on the Mediterranean Sea, north of Caesarea.

12.8.12.en: Goiim: it means the nations, and it lies in Gilgal beside Jericho.

12.8.14.en: Each of these cities had a number of villages and small towns belonging to it.

12.8.15.en: The group of kings mentioned reigned over this land, and their number was thirty-one kings, each reigning over one of the cities, and Joshua defeated all of them in the wars previously recounted in the book.

12.8.16.en: The portion of the tribes east of the Jordan. From this chapter until chapter nineteen, the book makes clear the portion of each tribe from the Promised Land.

12.8.17.en: This chapter is concerned with defining, in general, the land that the Lord granted to His people west of the Jordan, and then explaining in detail the borders of each of the two and a half tribes who took their portion east of the Jordan.

12.8.18.en: (1) The remaining land west of the Jordan in general (vv. 1-7:) 1 Now Joshua was old and stricken in years; and the Lord said unto him, “Thou art old and stricken in years, and there remaineth yet very much land to be possessed. 2 This is the land that yet remaineth: all the borders of the Philistines, and all Geshuri, 3 From Sihor, which is before Egypt, even unto the borders of Ekron northward, which is counted (to the Canaanite): five lords of the Philistines; the Gazathites, and the Ashdothites, the Eshkalonites, the Gittites, and the Ekronites; also the Avites: 4 From the south, all the land of the Canaanites, and Mearah that is beside the Sidonians, unto Aphek, to the borders of the Amorites: 5 And the land of the Giblites, and all Lebanon, toward the sunrising, from Baalgad under mount Hermon unto the entering into Hamath. 6 All the inhabitants of the hill country from Lebanon unto Misrephoth-maim, and all the Sidonians, them will I drive out from before the children of Israel: only divide thou it by lot unto the Israelites for an inheritance, as I have commanded thee. 7 Now therefore divide this land for an inheritance unto the nine tribes, and the half tribe of Manasseh.”
